subject: ClearMatch discovery — evaluation options & version safety
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Cole <erin@clearmatch.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearMatch discovery — evaluation options & version safety

Hi Erin,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning — really helpful to hear more about ClearMatch's name/identity normalization and question-answer flows for payment reconciliation. Per our call, I wanted to capture a concise next-steps plan and initial recommendations so your team can move to an evaluation quickly.

Summary of requirements we heard
- High precision on token-level entity extraction (names, account IDs) with low hallucination risk
- <= 150ms p50 tail for the smaller high-frequency endpoints; higher latency OK for batch re-processing jobs
- Auditability: retain per-request traces and prompt/response snapshots for 90 days

Redwood recommendation (start here)
- Model candidate: Open-Lite 13B (quant-8) — best balance of cost/latency for your 60M monthly tokens estimate
- For high-assurance name extraction routes, run a parallel test with Open-Safety 7B pinned to v1.4 for regression-sensitivity checks
- Suggested prompt set: provided in the attached clearmatch_eval_promptset_v1.zip (includes golden examples, adversarial cases, and the QA template you can run locally)

Benchmarks and assets
- Synthetic benchmark and prompt-set pass/fail criteria: attached (2026-09-14-benchmarks.md)
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-ExampleSharedEval

Version-safety note (important)
- There was a platform model roll last week that changed the default Open-Lite 13B kernel. Early signs in our internal regressions: slight ID-mangling for edge-case tokens in very long prompts. To avoid disruption, we recommend either:
  1) Pinning the model to the previous release (Open-Lite 13B @ r202606) for your production routes until the eval completes, or
  2) Enabling the automated fallback policy so requests that fail heuristics route to Open-Safety 7B (pinned).

If you want us to pin on our side for the trial, we can ship a pin request and a rollback window. Pinning is reversible and we can scope a canary for 48 hours on a small percentage of traffic.

Proposed next steps
- You: confirm the model(s) you want in the eval (Open-Lite 13B / Open-Safety 7B) and whether you want us to pin production during the trial
- We: share a short eval runbook and load script, and schedule a 30-min ops sync for onboarding the prompt set (I can do Fri 16:00 PT)

I'll also loop in our Ops/Model team for the pin details if you give the thumbs up.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0114

Attachments: clearmatch_eval_promptset_v1.zip (54kb), 2026-09-14-benchmarks.md (12kb)
From: Erin Cole <erin@clearmatch.com>

Cc: procurement@clearmatch.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:03:21 -0400
Subject: Re: ClearMatch discovery — evaluation options & version safety

Jonas —

Thanks for the recap and the clear options. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- We'd like to start the eval with Open-Lite 13B as primary and the Open-Safety 7B as a conservative comparator for the name extraction route.
- Yes, please pin Open-Lite 13B for the trial window — we can't afford any surprise shifts in behavior during our initial QA sprint. Please confirm what that means for response latency and how rollback would be executed.
- Procurement has been looped in for the terms. They requested a short statement that pinning is non-destructive and can be undone without data loss (we'll accept a sentence in email).

Also: can you add the sample prompts into a single Doc (we prefer Google Doc) and a short instruction for how to run the benchmark harness? Procurement also asked for the SOC2 link and retention SLA info.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Erin
Erin Cole
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearMatch
erin@clearmatch.com
